correctness.rationale: Necessity uses a permanent size-at-least-three obstruction on either white part and the frozen identical-two-set boundary. Sufficiency supplies an explicit first force in every remaining index pattern, with n>=3 safeguarding the 1+1 case. Counting by total omitted vertices gives all five coefficients. Every feasible pair extends to distinct two-subsets, proving uniform inclusion-minimality. Centering the explicit quartic gives a biquadratic with two distinct negative squared roots exactly for n>=5. The actual embedded verifier exhaustively checks 1,398,080 colored subsets for n=3..10, with independent simultaneous-round corroboration and exact rational algebra; the universal quantifiers follow from proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The zero-forcing polynomial is a natural full-cardinality graph invariant. A complete structural description of every forcing set on a standard graph family gives infinitely many exact coefficients, not a parameter rename or mere scalar bound. The inclusion-minimality result has independent graph-structural significance, and the abrupt n=5 transition to four simple zeros on a single vertical line is a nonobvious exact analytic property not inferable from minimum zero forcing alone. All require the complete classification.
